clue.text: Sensational account of what sounds like a peaceful drink with American

indicators.note: the phrase asks us to say the next words out loud and spell what we hear

blocks.note: a mellow dram is a calm little glass of whisky
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A storyteller's thrilling tale about sharing a relaxing whisky with an American friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'mellow dram' runs into the first part of MELODRAMA; the American adds the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a story full of exaggerated, sensational incident and emotion.

clue.text: Intended to have miserable time

blocks.note: mean can describe something wretched or miserable
T is the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone who deliberately set out to have a wretched time.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is the past tense of mean, a synonym of intended, as in 'I meant to call'.

clue.text: John is in later version

indicators.note: a new version of something is a reworked form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words are taken together

explanation.surface: John, a man, turns up in a later edition of something.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a man's name, but it is informal slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A john is slang for a toilet, and a latrine is a basic communal toilet.

clue.text: Daughter took one that was finished

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter picked up an item that had been completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Done as an adjective means completed or over, the same as finished.

clue.text: Voice raised in Scotland

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following word
in a down clue, raising letters means reading them upwards, bottom to top

blocks.note: the middle letters of the word, before reading them upwards

explanation.surface: A voice lifted in song somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Read sCOTLAnd from the end and ALTO appears in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a singing voice, the lowest female or highest adult male range.

clue.text: Symbolic tales in which friends capture dreadful ogre

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled
to capture is to hold something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: allies are friends who side with you
the letters of the monster rearranged

explanation.surface: Fables in which a band of friends seize a frightening ogre.
explanation.walkthrough: Capture looks like plot action in the fable, but it tells you the friends' word wraps round the jumbled monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegories are stories whose characters and events stand for deeper moral or political meanings.

clue.text: Investigated the fourth lawsuit

blocks.note: a case is a lawsuit heard in court
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone looked into the fourth legal action in a series.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists 'the fourth' first, but its letter goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To case a place is slang for inspecting it, typically before a robbery.

clue.text: Special hat designed for Moslem leaders

definitions.note: a caliphate is strictly the office or realm of a caliph rather than the leader himself

indicators.note: something designed is newly arranged or made, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words are taken together

explanation.surface: A particular piece of headgear made for Muslim leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliphates are the offices and states of caliphs, the historical rulers of the Muslim community.

clue.text: Tabloid on the French politician might be worth a tanner

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
la is a French word for the
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A cheap newspaper's story about a French politician, valued at sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is old British slang for a sixpence coin, but here it is something that tans you.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunlamp gives an artificial tan, so it serves as a tanner, a device that browns the skin.

clue.text: A number of events, then a cold spell

indicators.note: to spell is to set out letters in an order, so these letters get a new order

blocks.note: the letters of all three words are taken together

explanation.surface: Several things happened, and afterwards came a stretch of chilly weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A cold spell' reads as weather; spell is the anagram signal. The number of events is ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is an athletics contest made up of ten separate track and field events.

clue.text: Place to check on delivery times?

definitions.text: Place to check on delivery times?

blocks.clueFragment: Place to check on delivery times?
blocks.note: surface reading: a depot or post office where you look up when parcels arrive
setter's reading: the delivery of a baby, monitored before birth

explanation.walkthrough: Delivery suggests post or couriers, but it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Pregnant women attend this kind of clinic for checks before they give birth.

clue.text: Can accommodate Henry being somewhat anorexic

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a tin is a can
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Questioning whether there is room for Henry, who is rather underweight.
explanation.walkthrough: Can looks like a verb but is the noun, a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anorexic is extremely thin, so mildly anorexic suggests simply thin.

clue.text: Encourage scheme to start trading in the vegetable

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: to egg on is to encourage
a plan is a scheme
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Urging a business plan to begin dealing in vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggplant is the American name for the aubergine, a purple-skinned vegetable.

clue.text: Coagulates around lists

indicators.note: letters moved around end up in a different arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of the word taken whole

explanation.surface: Something thickening around a set of inventories.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is a systematic list of items, so catalogues are lists.

clue.text: Uncoil bits moving in pubs'' bins

indicators.note: the pieces of the word are on the move, so they settle in a new order
in places the jumbled letters inside the next word

blocks.note: bars are pubs
the letters of the word rearranged

explanation.surface: Uncoiling scraps tossed into the rubbish bins behind pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bins suggests rubbish, but it is British slang for binoculars. The jumbled letters go between B and ARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bins is informal British slang for binoculars, the paired magnifying glasses.

clue.text: Upset to leave rich knight

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words are taken together

explanation.surface: A knight annoyed at having to leave wealth behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalier is a French title for a knight or member of an order of chivalry.

clue.text: Holdall favoured by the out-of-town candidate?

definitions.note: a description of the bag rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a travelling bag made of carpet fabric
second meaning: the bag that gave its name to outsiders seeking office

explanation.walkthrough: After the US Civil War, northerners who went south seeking political office were called carpetbaggers, after their luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: This luggage is a holdall, and carpetbagger means a politician standing somewhere they have no local roots.

clue.text: Papal order shock

indicators.note: putting letters in a fresh order rearranges them

blocks.note: the letters of the word taken whole

explanation.surface: A decree from the Pope causes outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papal order' looks like a decree from the Pope; order is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay, a strong synonym of shock as a verb.

clue.text: Port and two thirds of a glass of Spanish wine

indicators.note: keeping two thirds of a three-letter word means dropping its final letter

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port
a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: Port wine plus most of a glass of Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the fortified drink, matching the wine theme, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Moronic use of Greek letter

indicators.note: making use of letters means working them into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of the word taken whole

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly misusing a character from the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a short O.

clue.text: Been greedy, love? Never eat crumble!

indicators.note: something that crumbles breaks into bits that can be put back differently

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
the letters of both words rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling a darling who has stuffed themselves never to eat crumble, the pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumble looks like the fruit pudding but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have overeaten is to have eaten too much, which is behaving greedily.

clue.text: Run into Pooh's cat and pull the lever

indicators.note: into places one piece inside another

blocks.note: Tigger is the bouncy tiger in the Winnie-the-Pooh stories
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bump into Tigger from Winnie-the-Pooh and then pull a lever.
explanation.walkthrough: Tigger is a tiger, a big cat, so cat stands for him.
explanation.definitionFit: A trigger is the small lever pulled to fire a gun or set off a mechanism.

clue.text: The last word in religious broadcasting

definitions.note: names the type of programme rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a closing speech or section at the end of a work
second meaning: a short religious programme that once closed British TV each night

explanation.walkthrough: The Epilogue was the brief religious talk that ended the BBC and ITV broadcasting day in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is a concluding section, the closing words of a play or book.

clue.text: Fail to catch the girl

blocks.note: first meaning: to not hit or grab something
second meaning: a title or term for a young woman

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a lost romantic chance; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both failing to hit or catch and a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Give the letters of a magic formula

blocks.note: first meaning: to name the letters of a word in order
second meaning: an incantation with magical power

explanation.surface: Someone asked to recite each letter of a magic incantation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both naming letters in order and a set of words believed to work magic.

clue.text: After a couple, one can make it

definitions.text: After a couple, one can make it

blocks.clueFragment: After a couple, one can make it
blocks.note: surface reading: once a pair is together, a single person can succeed or arrive
setter's reading: one more added to a pair forms a group of three

explanation.walkthrough: Couple and make it suggest romance or success, but the clue is just counting: two plus one.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three things or people is so called, which is a couple plus one.

clue.text: Am back at home, chief!

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word from its end

blocks.note: the word read in the opposite direction
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Someone announcing to the boss that they've returned home.
explanation.definitionFit: Main as an adjective means principal or most important, the same as chief.

clue.text: The fateful shape for an island?

definitions.text: The fateful shape for an island?

blocks.clueFragment: The fateful shape for an island?
blocks.note: surface reading: an odd question about the doomed outline of an island
setter's reading: a three-sided figure named after an Atlantic island, notorious for lost ships

explanation.walkthrough: A shape named after an island is a triangle with an island's name; fateful points to the legend of vanishing ships and planes.
explanation.definitionFit: This region of the western Atlantic, bounded by three points, is famed for mysterious disappearances.

clue.text: Heartlessly going for second lot of medals …

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its middle
S is the standard abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Ruthlessly going for a second batch of medals.
explanation.walkthrough: Gongs is British slang for medals or honours.
explanation.definitionFit: Gongs is informal British slang for medals and decorations, so a set of them.

clue.text: … seen, namely, round about the Spanish villain

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are moved into a new arrangement

blocks.note: sc. abbreviates Latin scilicet, meaning namely
the letters of the word rearranged
el is a Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: medals spotted on a Spanish rogue doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses join this clue to 26, so the medals are seen on a villain; seen just links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest, unscrupulous person, which is a villain.
